text:
maria: Heads-up — saw a persistent p95 spike (2.3x) on shared-pool-c starting ~03:10 UTC after last runtime rollout. It correlates with tenant t-12 workloads. :thinking:

alex: ugh. do you have traces/heatmap?

maria: attaching quick summary from grafana: kv-hit drops from 78% -> 11% during spike, queue-length and batching latency both increase.

jun: that kv-hit collapse screams cache thrash/eviction. did rollout change cache slot count or eviction policy?

maria: rollout included kernel-selection tweak + smaller batching window for latency-sensitive routes. no direct kv config changes.

perf-bot: Sampling started: profile_id=pf_20260312_0315 pool=shared-pool-c duration=10m

alex: ran a quick flamegraph against pf_20260312_0315 — lots of time in fallback kernel path (fused_attn_fp32_fallback) instead of quantized path.

jun: interesting — kernel selector might be flipping because observed sequence_len distribution spiked for tenant t-12 (long prompts). Batching heuristic packs long + short tasks -> kernel mismatch and KV thrash.

sara: can you paste the selector log lines?

alex: sure:
```
[03:12:01] kernel_selector: candidate=[fast_q_fused, fast_q_attn_kv]
[03:12:01] runtime-decide: seq_len=1536, batch-seq-stdev=680 -> chosen=fallback_fp32_fused
[03:12:01] kv_cache: evict_slots=42 active_slots=18 -> hit_rate=0.12
```

maria: so heuristic treats mixed seq batches as unsafe and picks fp32 fallback which is much slower + increases KV slot churn because fallback uses different cache layout.

jun: that matches profiling: fallback kernel increases per-token latency by ~3x and allocs extra KV metadata which reduces effective cache capacity. Noisy tenant with large seqs can starve small ones.

sara: is this new behavior introduced by the rollout or was it latent?

alex: regression window points to commit a1b2c3 (kernel-selector: use stdev threshold 600 -> 400). Lower threshold makes selector more conservative -> picks fallback more often.

maria: ok, actionable: revert threshold for the hot pool or add per-tenant seq histogram gating. Suggest immediate rollback on pool-c and create a canary with per-tenant gating.

deploy-bot: rollout a1b2c3 rolled back on pool=shared-pool-c at 03:40 UTC by @maria

jun: post-rollback check — kv-hit recovered to ~75% and p95 back to normal within 3 minutes. Looks good.

sara: follow-ups: (1) add a metric for selector_fallback_rate by tenant, (2) add KV slot usage alert when hit_rate<20% and eviction_rate>30/min, (3) update selector to consider per-tenant pinned_kv footprint before choosing kernel.

alex: I'll open PR for selector change and add the metric. will tag perf for review.

maria: filing incident doc and linking traces. Thanks everyone. :pray:

perf-bot: perf report attached -> https://perf.internal/reports/pf_20260312_0315

maria: incident thread closed for now — monitoring the canary. If we see >5% fallback_rate for any tenant for 5m, will auto-scale dedicated for that tenant.

alex: noted, will follow up with PR link in a few hours.

sara: great, moving to postmortem. high-level cause: kernel-selector threshold regression -> increased fallback kernel usage -> KV cache thrash -> noisy-tenant-induced latency spike.

maria: recording action items in incident board. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
